summary: Construction that results in a capital improvement is contracting, not taxed to the customer; the contractor pays tax on its purchases.

citations.quote: If the end result of the service is a capital improvement to real property, the service is considered to be "contracting" and is not taxable.

notes: The cited statutes were last amended in 2017 or earlier (bill histories on code.wvlegislature.gov), so 2018-01-01 is the earliest date read here; the treatment is older. summary: Repair or maintenance of real property that is not a capital improvement is a taxable service: tax on labor and materials.
